title: Follow each change in What's new
body: What's new shows each change with its date, category and a link to the relevant page. Entries are grouped by month, with the full change history available again.

title: Unreadable encryption is shown as Not assessed
body: A device whose disk encryption could not be read now shows Not assessed on its Compliance tab, not Fail.

title: Clearer labels for Overview's CVE action
body: Overview's top CVE action now labels its count as critical or high CVEs for the named product.

title: Clearer release sources in Version sprawl
body: The latest released version now shows its source in plain English and when it was checked. Where a source link is available, you can open it from the report.

title: Safer CSV downloads
body: CSV downloads of Devices, Findings and Homebrew packages now protect against spreadsheet formula injection, as the AI Tooling and Local admins downloads already did. A value that could run as a formula when opened in a spreadsheet is shown as plain text. The PDF downloads are unchanged.

title: Install tokens are for administrators
body: One-off install tokens can now only be generated by administrators on your account. Everyone else still sees the Install page and the estate enrolment keys, with a note to ask an administrator.

title: Download any list as a PDF
body: Every list that offered a CSV download now offers a PDF too, including Devices, Jamf coverage, Findings, Homebrew, Local admins, AI Tooling and the software reports. The PDF shows the same rows as the CSV for the same filters, with the filters listed at the top. Very long lists show the first 10,000 rows and say how many there are in total.

title: Download every report as a PDF or a CSV
body: Each report you generate now comes as both a PDF and a CSV, including scheduled reports. Use Download CSV in the Report history when you want the figures in a spreadsheet. Reports generated before today stay PDF only; generate them again to get a CSV.

title: Approve software before it appears in your estate
body: Estate administrators can now add approved software before any device reports it, and see it on Software as not observed until one does. An approval records your decision only. It does not show the software is installed, trusted or compliant, and it never hides a vulnerability.

title: Clearer Support and Feedback
body: Use Support for problems and questions, with a short form, optional screenshot and email fallback. Feedback is for feature requests and design or usability improvements. Each page shows the status of its own submissions.

title: Track expiry for public certificates
body: Certificates brings uploaded public certificates and agent-reported certificates into one expiry view. Estate administrators can label, replace and remove uploads while missing expiry evidence stays explicit.

title: Overview opens when no new software has been found
body: Overview now loads correctly when the reported new-software window is empty, including for a new estate. Software risk that cannot be read still shows as unavailable.

title: Download your Cyber Essentials evidence pack
body: Cyber Essentials readiness now offers a dated PDF with per-device update and control evidence, sources and observation times. Missing or stale evidence stays explicit, and the pack does not provide a certification verdict.

title: Pages that work best on a larger screen now say so on a phone
body: On a phone, the detailed pages such as Software, Findings and the device tabs now say under their heading that they are best viewed on a larger screen. The Overview, Alerts, a device's own page, My requests and Feedback stay laid out for a phone.

title: Compliance descriptions without internal references
body: Compliance descriptions now omit internal tracking references while retaining each control's assessment criteria.

title: Consistent OS update counts across your estate
body: Overview and executive reports now use the same collected OS verdicts as Devices. Unknown or stale verdicts stay unconfirmed, so an older empty update list cannot make the collective view look up to date.

title: Clearer missing update evidence
body: Windows and macOS device views now explain when a device has not reported a recent update state. Reported update verdicts and stale-device warnings stay distinct.

title: Unknown update counts on Overview
body: Overview now includes the Unknown count in Update currency. A missing or invalid count reads Not reported, while an explicit zero stays zero.

title: OS update status keeps missing evidence explicit
body: Device update status now respects the latest collected OS verdict. Unknown or stale evidence stays unconfirmed rather than appearing up to date because an older update list was empty.

title: OS versions on the device roster
body: Devices now shows reported OS versions and builds at every screen size, with last-seen evidence beside device identity and compact assurance summaries. Missing versions remain clearly marked as not reported.

title: A more compact device overview
body: Device details now keep identity and assurance together, with counts in the section tabs. Collection issues and their help links remain prominent, with issue dates available on demand.

title: Review AI tooling in a compact list
body: AI Tooling now uses the compact review controls from Software, with filters that survive sharing or reloading. Open a product name for its AI evidence and approval history; collection by device is an optional view with 25 devices per page.

title: Installed versions stay visible in Software
body: Software review rows now show labelled installed versions below each product name. Missing version evidence and unknown installation counts remain explicit, with full version values available when a list is shortened.

title: Sort and export your local admin view
body: Filter and search local admins by account or device, then sort the results and export that exact view. Shared links keep your filters and order, and the full estate export is still available separately.

title: See installed versions alongside finding targets
body: CVE findings now show the reported installed version beside the separately labelled target at desktop and phone widths. Missing installed evidence is explicitly shown as Not reported.

title: Filter devices by type
body: The Devices page can now show only servers or only workstations within each reporting state. Servers are identified in the Platform column, without an extra label beside the hostname.

title: Device software versions stay together
body: Long version numbers on a device's Software tab now stay on one line. Lists of versions wrap between values, so each version remains easy to read on a phone too.

title: Software CSV exports download in full again
body: Software report CSV exports now download in full. The same fix keeps other CSV exports and PDF report downloads complete when they pass through a compression proxy.

title: Read full software names and publishers
body: Software publishers and Homebrew package names and taps now show their full value when you hover over shortened text.

title: Device AI tooling opens without a recorded launch
body: A device's AI tooling page now opens when an application has no recorded launch time. Invalid or inconsistent evidence is still withheld, with a clear explanation on the page.

title: See which software is unused from the Software page
body: Software now shows whether each product is Used, Unused or Not metered, with when it was last used, and More filters has a Usage filter that lists only the unused software. Software Patched could not measure, or has only partial evidence for, never counts as unused.

title: Servers are now marked on the Devices page
body: A Windows Server now reads Windows Server in the Platform column, carries a Server tag beside its hostname, and shows its release, such as Server 2022, before the build number. A device's own page has a Type row and the Devices CSV has a new Type column, and searching for server finds them. Servers are not scored against a CIS benchmark yet, so their CIS score reads n/a rather than a percentage. Their failing checks come from Patched's baseline checks.

title: My requests lines up properly
body: The list of feedback you have sent now has aligned columns and spacing, so the Received and Last update dates no longer run together and each status sits under its heading. On a phone, each request now shows as a labelled block.

title: Dates stay on one line across the portal
body: A date in a table or an evidence list could break across two lines, for example in the Verification column of a device's Compliance tab, the drivers list on Findings and the software reports. Each date now stays on one line, and the surrounding text still wraps.

title: Clearer Duplicate tools and Version sprawl reports
body: The Duplicate tools report now explains its second rule in plain words: two or more paid products in a category needs licence data and is not applied yet. On a phone, the Version sprawl report no longer lets one product's details run into the next row.

title: Device page now agrees with the Devices list
body: A device's failing checks now come from the same count on the Devices list and on its own page, so the two always agree. The Summary on a device's page now shows its real disk encryption and update state, including Windows update state, where it used to say Not assessed.

title: Clearer Devices list and device page
body: The Devices list no longer shows an unreported update state on every Windows row: it says once that Patched does not show update state for Windows devices yet, and its pills no longer run into the Last seen column. The CIS score now shows as a percentage, a device's failing checks match between the list and its own page, and Windows version numbers stay on one line.

title: Review software one line at a time
body: Each product in Software is now a single line: its name with the publisher beside it, installs and versions, CVE assessment, signing, and one approval state (Unreviewed, Approved, Unapproved or Ignored) with the control to change it. After you set a state you stay on the same filtered list with the next product in view, and you can tick several products to mark them at once. Select a product's name to see its history and identifiers.

title: Software's waiting count matches the Overview
body: The count at the top of Software is now the Overview's own figure for products waiting on an approval decision, stated plainly and steady between loads. Filters and searches are kept in the page address, so links from the Overview open the list already filtered, and the new since your last review notice opens those products as a list to work through.

title: Homebrew uses the same filters as Software
body: Homebrew now has the same filter bar as Software, with type, approval, install type and findings kept in the page address. A package with no matched CVE now reads Not yet assessed instead of an empty cell, which could be mistaken for a clean result.

title: Overview figures now agree with each other
body: The number of products waiting on a decision is now the same in Top 3 actions, Your estate at a glance and the Software awaiting approval card. The page heading reads Overview, with your organisation's name beneath it, and the Reporting and agent health card now says its figure counts devices with a collection issue.

title: Review new software in Software
body: The Overview's New software card is now a read only summary. Its urgency counts, product names and decision links open Software, where you approve, mark as not wanted or ignore a product, instead of setting a state from the Overview.

title: Known vulnerable drivers on Windows devices
body: A device's Compliance tab now lists any of its kernel drivers matched against Microsoft's recommended driver block rules and loldrivers.io, with the source list, version, fetch date and matching hash, whether the driver is loaded, and whether Windows' vulnerable driver blocklist is enforced. Findings now has a matching estate-wide section, with a filter for devices where the blocklist is not enforced.

title: Your device list card is easier to check
body: The device list card on Devices now leads with three tiles (Matched, Not reporting, Reporting not on your list) that filter the table below with no need for JavaScript. The Matched group lists each uploaded entry against the device it matched, including whether that device is retired. A device on your list that has not reported can now be removed directly from the row, or you can send it to install the agent instead. Upload details sit on one line in the header, and the Serial column only shows when a row actually has one.

title: Cyber insurance evidence pack
body: Reports now answers the endpoint questions on a typical cyber insurance renewal form from Patched's evidence, with the source and date of every answer and the devices it could not speak for, and lists the questions Patched cannot answer so none is missed. Download it as a PDF or CSV.

title: Local admins page under Governance
body: A new Local admins page lists every account holding standing local administrator rights across your estate, by account or by device, with estate tiles for devices over the admin limit, distinct accounts and devices whose membership could not be read. A directory group is labelled as a group, not a person, and an unresolved SID is shown as unresolved rather than guessed at. Filters by platform, principal type, admin count and membership, plus a CSV export.

title: Firmware details on the device Hardware tab
body: Windows devices with an up to date agent now show BIOS, system and baseboard details on their Hardware tab, including BIOS vendor, version and release age. Mac firmware is not shown separately, since it is updated together with macOS.

title: Tidier High-risk software and Browser extensions cards
body: The Overview's High-risk software and Browser extensions cards now sit as a balanced pair with clearer figures, a short preview of the most notable items and one clear action each, instead of a tall list on one side and empty space on the other.

title: Clearer AI Tooling summary and filters
body: AI Tooling now opens with four clear estate tiles instead of six, led by what needs review, with local runtimes and MCP servers folded into one Local AI tile. The Products table filters by type, state and assessment from one search-and-filter bar with removable chips, and the notifications card saves both settings from a single Save.

title: Estate enrolment keys for MDM rollouts
body: Install now offers reusable estate enrolment keys alongside the existing one-off install token, so an admin can roll the agent out to many devices from one Intune, Jamf or RMM deployment instead of minting a token per device. Keys show a device cap, expiry and status, and can be revoked at any time; the plaintext key is shown once, on creation, and never again.

title: Feedback sends every time
body: Suggest a feature and Ask a question now send correctly, and the bug impact question only shows for bug reports. If a Feedback form has been open a long time, what you typed is kept and sent rather than lost to a reload.

title: Cyber Essentials readiness page
body: A new Cyber Essentials readiness page lists what stands between each device and the Cyber Essentials v3.3 14-day update rule, plus the malware protection, firewall and secure configuration controls Patched can evidence. It states what the evidence shows, not a certification, and exports to CSV.

title: Clearer Overview card colours and CIS score
body: Overview cards now show the CIS score rounded, and only use green when there is genuinely nothing to act on.

title: New software report
body: A New software report on the Reports page lists everything first seen on your estate since your last review, with a quick approve or unapprove from the row. A callout at the top of Software tells you how many are waiting, and admins can turn the new-software notification on or off from the report itself. Exports to CSV and PDF.

title: Unapproved and unreviewed software report
body: A new drift report on the Reports page shows the current Unapproved and Unreviewed software list, a 26-week trend and the devices carrying the most unapproved software. Exports to CSV and PDF, alongside a one-click approved-software list export.

title: Estate summary cards on Overview
body: Overview now opens with ten summary cards covering devices, updates, vulnerabilities, CIS posture, browser extensions, high-risk and awaiting-approval software, exceptions, reporting health and recent activity. Each card links straight to the matching detail view, and shows plainly when something is not yet known or not available rather than guessing.

title: AI tooling evidence and governance
body: AI Tooling now shows recognised products, approval and vulnerability-assessment state, exact last-used evidence where available, collector coverage and secret-safe per-device detail. You can export up to 1,000 products from one complete snapshot, govern individual or selected items, and manage AI-tooling first-seen notifications independently; missing or failed collection stays visibly unknown rather than reading as clean.

title: Send feedback from the portal
body: You can now report a problem, suggest an improvement or ask a question from any portal page. Track what you sent and its current status in My requests.

title: Footer no longer covers portal content
body: The desktop footer now waits until the end of the page instead of covering cards and controls while you scroll. The navigation rail remains available independently.

title: Clearer portal typography and attention details
body: Headings, labels, controls and status badges now use the clearer Patched interface type. Overview attention items are now compact, clearly separated and easier to scan on every screen size.

title: AI Tooling preview added
body: An In development placeholder now shows where the future AI Tooling evidence view will live and explains its planned collection boundary. It contains no AI inventory data or controls yet.

title: A clearer Brand v3 portal
body: The portal now uses Patched's blue Brand v3 system throughout, including the approved circular P, a calmer navy navigation rail, clearer primary actions and stronger Overview hierarchy. Your underlying estate data and workflows are unchanged.

title: Overview puts ongoing software and extension risk first
body: The Overview now shows what we can see of your estate first, then a High-risk software card with the reasons each newly found product was flagged, and a Browser extensions card with elevated-risk extensions and those waiting on a decision. Once no critical or high CIS check is failing, CIS folds into a compact posture card, with the full detail one click away.

title: Jamf Pro coverage
body: Devices now includes a Jamf coverage page comparing the Macs your Jamf Pro manages with the Macs Patched sees, built from webhooks your Jamf Pro sends. It shows Macs Jamf manages that Patched has not seen, Macs Patched sees that Jamf has not reported, and connector health, with CSV download and a setup page for the webhook token. Patched never holds a Jamf credential.

title: Duplicate tools and software publisher reports
body: Reports now includes a duplicate tools report, showing categories where your estate runs several competing products for the same job, and a software publishers report, grouping every installed application by the publisher its code signing evidence proves, with installs Patched cannot verify shown first. Both include a CSV download.

title: Remote access and version sprawl reports
body: Reports now includes a remote access tools report, showing every remote access tool on your estate with its approval state and your own RMM agents kept separate, plus a version sprawl report showing how many versions of each application are live and how they compare with the latest released version. Both include a CSV download.

title: Unsupported software report
body: Reports now includes an unsupported software report: every installed product and operating system version past its vendor's end of support, or within 90 days of it, by device, with a Cyber Essentials evidence summary and a CSV download.

title: Approve Homebrew packages too
body: Formulae and casks on the Homebrew tab can now be approved, unapproved or ignored just like other software, with Unreviewed and Unapproved counts at the top of the page.

title: Retire a device yourself
body: You can now retire and reactivate a device directly on its device page or from the Devices list, with an optional reason. A retired device stays on your roster and is never counted as missing.

title: Upload your own device list
body: Upload a CSV of your devices on the Devices page to see which ones you expect but have not seen, and which reporting devices are not on your list yet.

title: Your estate at a glance
body: The Overview now opens with a short summary of your estate and up to three recommended actions, each linking straight to the page you need to act on.

title: Device pages, organised into tabs
body: Device pages are now organised into tabs (Overview, Hardware, Software, Vulnerabilities, Compliance, Evidence), so each part of a device is one click away.

title: Tidier device and Overview layouts
body: Device pages line their details up properly, list storage without the clutter of macOS system volumes, and show small sizes in MB. The Overview's attention rows are easier to scan.

title: What needs attention, at a glance
body: The Overview now shows failing CIS checks and confirmed CVEs as colour-coded severity counts in one card, and the New software card only appears when there is new software to review.

title: Device pages lead with what matters
body: Each device page now opens with its CVE and CIS issue counts, which jump to the details when clicked, then one card with the device's identity and evidence side by side and a tighter hardware summary.

title: Filter software your way
body: Filter software your way: pick a type and any combination of approval states from simple dropdowns, and remove a filter with one tap.

title: Support always within reach
body: On a desktop, the footer and the Support contact now stay at the bottom of the screen as you scroll, so help is always one click away.

title: A clearer Alerts page
body: The Alerts page is easier to scan: dates fit on two lines, each tab shows only the columns it needs, and you can search by product name or pick a device instead of typing an ID.

title: Software installed on one device
body: See everything installed on one device: open a device and choose Software installed.

title: Device identity and hardware
body: Every device page now shows the machine's identity and hardware: serial number, model, operating system build, processor, memory, disks, storage and battery health.

title: Phone-friendly tables
body: Tables on the device page and the Homebrew page now stack into readable rows on a phone instead of squeezing sideways.

title: Overview approvals stay on the Overview
body: Approving software from the Overview now keeps you on the Overview, and software waiting on a decision no longer drops off the Software page.

title: New software card, colour coded
body: The Overview's New software card is now colour coded by urgency, so the most pressing software stands out at a glance.

title: Decide on software yourself
body: Approve, unapprove or ignore software on the Software page, one at a time or in bulk. Every decision is kept in a history of who decided what and when.

title: Unapproved software alerts
body: Unapproved software found on your estate now raises an alert you can acknowledge on the Alerts page. It resolves itself once the software is gone or approved.

title: New software flagged by urgency
body: The Overview's New software card shows software newly found on your estate, sorted by urgency so the riskiest items stand out first.

title: Why evidence is incomplete
body: Device pages now explain why their evidence is incomplete, for example a missing macOS permission, so you know what to fix.

title: Clearer CVE assessment
body: Every product on the Software page now shows its CVE assessment: no known CVEs, a count, still checking, or not yet assessed. Not yet assessed is never shown as clean.
